truth.purpose: A Python library that cryptographically signs (HMAC) serialized data so it can be sent through untrusted places such as cookies, URLs or emailed links, and verified as untampered (optionally not expired) when it comes back.
truth.audience: Python web developers who need tamper-proof tokens, e.g. for sessions, password-reset or account-activation links.
derived_from: repo tree (src/itsdangerous: signer, serializer, timed, url_safe)

response.what_it_does: A Python library that signs data (e.g. a dict) with a secret key so you can hand it to an untrusted client as a token and later verify it wasn't tampered with, with optional timestamps and compression.
response.who_its_for: Python web developers who need to pass signed tokens (auth, session-like data, links) between requests.

What crypto is used (HMAC? which hash?) is not stated; 'cryptographically signed' is vague
Is data encrypted or only signed? Readers might assume secrecy; text doesn't clarify
No badges or text showing maturity, maintenance, or tests; the name and tagline 'so better sign this' are cutesy
'Data is compressed as needed' is vague
